target_customer: Product design and engineering teams that hand finished UI designs to developers
problem: Designers and developers lost time passing design specs, assets and style details between design tools and code. Zeplin published finished designs with measurements, assets and code snippets so developers did not have to ask.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription per team or seat
product_category: Design handoff and design delivery workspace

founders.name: Pelin Kenez
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch (2015-11-24) says the team previously worked at a mobile company where they handled designer to developer handoffs; employer not named.

founders.name: Ismail Ceylan
founders.role: Founder, software developer (COO per YC page)
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page; background not found.

founders.name: Merih Akar
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page; background not found.

founders.name: Berk Çebi
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page; background not found.

competitors.name: InVision (Inspect)
competitors.what: Prototyping and design collaboration platform that added code and spec inspection for Sketch designs
competitors.traction_then: Named by TechCrunch as the main existing alternative; Inspect for Craft was mentioned in a September 2015 post

competitors.name: Adobe
competitors.what: Design tool maker that TechCrunch said could build a similar handoff tool

technical_complexity.rationale: A Sketch plugin plus a web and Mac app that exports specs and assets; standard engineering for a small team in 2015.

defensibility.rationale: Early handoff tool with team workflows, but design tools and rivals such as InVision could add inspection features, as later happened with Figma Dev Mode.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: InVision shipped Inspect in 2015 and 2016 and later design tools added native handoff; Zeplin stayed independent and added a second product, Omlet.

market_need_then: Sketch based design workflows were growing fast in 2015 and developers lacked reliable specs; TechCrunch described handoff between designers and engineers as the pain Zeplin addressed.

branding.name_origin: The company's about page says the team wrote a script that listed Turkish words resembling English words, wanting a name anyone could read and say, and they liked the word.
branding.domain_note: Uses zeplin.io rather than a .com; no acquisition story found.

identity.logo: Airship illustration beside uppercase ZEPLIN wordmark, per a logo database
identity.visual_style: Bold sans serif wordmark with orange, yellow and blue palette per a color listing site (secondary source)

branding.brand_signature: Airship mark tied to the Turkish origin of the name
branding.community_and_virality: Used widely by designers and developers and covered in many tool comparisons; no fan or merch evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: Well known in design and developer circles and a default name in handoff comparisons, but no evidence of the brand itself driving growth beyond the product.

outcome_analysis: Zeplin launched version 1.0 in July 2015 during the Sketch boom, raised a $1.2M seed in November 2015 and reached 1 million users by October 2017 and 5 million by September 2022 per its own timeline. It stayed independent and active, opened a San Francisco office in 2016, and added a second product, Omlet, though built in handoff features from design tools are the main long term threat.
notes: FinSMEs independently reports the $1.2M seed in November 2015; one aggregator dates it December 2015 which looks like an error. Aggregators list total raised of $1.34M to $1.4M and extra investors (Y Combinator, Graph Ventures, Floodgate) that were not seen in a primary source. A third party profile claims 2024 revenue of $51.9M and 91 employees; unverified and not used. YC lists founded 2015 while the company timeline says June 2014. No Series A found; searches returned ZEPL, a different company. Outcome search found no acquisition or layoffs.
